newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's IFCT says ready to manage troubled bank.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's IFCT says ready to manage troubled bank.

text.p: The Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT) said on Friday it had finalised a plan to manage troubled and scandal-ridden Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc from May at the request of the Bank of Thailand.

An official at IFCT, an industrial financing bank owned 45 percent by the finance ministry and other government agencies and 33 percent by foreign institutional investors, said his firm planned to announce next week progress of talks with the central bank on its future management role in the bank.

Bangkok Bank of Commerce was taken over by the government last May after opposition politicians revealed in parliament that it was saddled with about 77 billion baht ($2.96 billion) of non-performing and doubtful debt.

Former top executives of the medium-sized bank, including ex-president Krirkkiat Jalichandra, have since faced charges of embezzlement and conspiring to defraud the bank by approving big loans with inflated collateral to associated business.

Thai police this month issued two arrest warrants for Saudi Arabian tycoon Adnan Khashoggi on suspicion that he had been helped by former bank executives to defraud the bank by tapping more than two billion baht in loans used for buying shares in Thai companies.
Khashoggi was quoted by the Saudi newspaper Al-Eqtisadiah of denying the charges, saying he was considering suing Thai authorities for defamation.

The IFCT official said his firm was prepared to start running the bank from May after its current shareholders, including The Financial Institution Development Fund (FIDF) run by the central bank, approved the rescue plan at its next scheduled meeting on April 30.

IFCT's proposed management of the bank followed a series of earlier unsuccessful government attempts to revive the bank, including abortive proposals for Thai finance firms to buy a controlling interest in the ailing bank.

Central bank officials said early this month that in return for managing the bank, IFCT would be offered an option to buy up to 51 percent of the bank's current 35 billion baht equity after having run it for three years.
They said IFCT would be given a seven-year management contract by the Bangkok Bank of Commerce on condition the bank's huge bad loans were first written off or absorbed by a new company.
The IFCT official declined to estimate the bank's outstanding non-performing loans, saying only that it would likely be over 80 billion baht.
He said: "We should not have any problem running the bank. FIDF is expected to inject any needed liquidity if it is required in the future."

An analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities Co said she expected the bank's bad loans to grow over time as its assets, including collateralised properties and stocks, deteriorated in line with a slowing Thai economy.

"I think IFCT could turn BBC into a profitable bank provided its bad loans were taken care of...but it would be difficult to find a private banker willing to take the daunting job as its new chief executive," the analyst said.
Central bank officials have said 10 IFCT representatives would sit on the Bangkok Bank of Commerce's new 15-member board if the industrial bank ran the bank.
